# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

  04_bump_rate_by_scorer     NVD raised the severity band: rate for the 15 biggest scorers of labelled CVEs
  05_drift_2026              (a) bump rate by month, val vs test; (b) precision of a val-tuned vs a label-free tau
The TabPFN vs HGB learning curve already exists (results/learning_curve.png, scripts/11 + 13) and is not redrawn.
Panel 05b refits HGB on all train rows (seed 0, CPU, ~1 min) because per-row predictions are not in results/.

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

AS_OF = (R / "data_as_of.txt").read_text().strip()

# reference palette (dataviz skill, light mode): slots 1-3 validate all-pairs

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.size": 11, "axes.titlesize": 14, "axes.titleweight": "bold", "axes.titlelocation": "left",

    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "axes.grid.axis": "y",

})

    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, caption, color=MUTED, fontsize=8.5, ha="left", va="bottom", wrap=True)
    fig.savefig(OUT / f"{name}.png", dpi=160)

    ax.bar(np.arange(len(FIELDS)) + (k - 1) * w, [dis[yr][f] * 100 for f in FIELDS], width=w - 0.03, color=col,

"""Error analysis (SPEC §10): 20 false-positive "likely" flags and 20 false negatives of the served combined model
(stack = TabPFN-3.5 + fine-tuned-LLM features, seed 0; results/serving_stack.json) on the 2026 evaluation test rows
of the frozen snapshot (results/data_as_of.txt). Writes results/error_sample.md for the human to tag [HUMAN].

  false positive  band "likely" (p >= tau, label-free top 10% of Deferred) and NVD did NOT raise the band
  false negative  NVD raised the band, but the band is not "likely" (shown: "possible" or "unlikely")
"Our vector" is what the product serves: the LLM vector if p >= gate t, else the CNA vector (final_table.md §4/§6).
The raw fine-tuned LLM vector is shown as well.

Needs the per-row stack predictions from scripts/12 (data/m4/tabpfn_llm_stack_s0.parquet, GPU workstation).
Usage: python scripts/10_error_analysis.py [--preds data/m4/tabpfn_llm_stack_s0.parquet] [--n 20]"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth.cvss import SEV, base_score, sev_rank  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--preds", default="data/m4/tabpfn_llm_stack_s0.parquet")
ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=20)
ap.add_argument("--out", default="results/error_sample.md")
a = ap.parse_args()

R = Path("results")
if not Path(a.preds).exists():
    sys.exit(f"{a.preds} not found: it is written by scripts/12_m4_experiments.py on the GPU workstation "
             "(config tabpfn_llm_stack, seed 0). Run this script there, or copy the file here.")
AS_OF = (R / "data_as_of.txt").read_text().strip()
serving = json.loads((R / "serving_stack.json").read_text())
tau, tau_possible, gate_t = serving["tau"], serving["tau_possible"], serving["gate_t"]
llm = json.loads((R / "llm_vectors_ft_test.json").read_text())

pr = pd.read_parquet(a.preds)
pr = pr[pr.split == "test"]
df = pd.read_parquet("data/cves.parquet").set_index("cve")
d = df.loc[pr.cve].copy()
d["p"] = pr.p.to_numpy()
assert (d.bump_up.astype(int).to_numpy() == pr.y.to_numpy()).all(), "labels differ from the M4 predictions"
assert len(d) == serving["test_eval_rows"]["n"], "not the 2026 evaluation rows of serving_stack.json"
d["band"] = np.where(d.p >= tau, "likely", np.where(d.p >= tau_possible, "possible", "unlikely"))
# sanity: same band counts as the served model's evidence file
for b, v in serving["test_eval_rows"]["bands"].items():
    assert int((d.band == b).sum()) == v["n"], f"band {b} count differs from serving_stack.json"
d["llm_vector"] = [llm.get(c) for c in d.index]
d["our_vector"] = np.where(d.p >= gate_t, d.llm_vector, d.cna_vector)
y = d.bump_up.astype(bool)

fp_pool = d[(d.band == "likely") & ~y]
fn_pool = d[y & (d.band != "likely")]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
fp = fp_pool.loc[rng.choice(fp_pool.index, size=min(a.n, len(fp_pool)), replace=False)].sort_values("p", ascending=False)
fn = fn_pool.loc[rng.choice(fn_pool.index, size=min(a.n, len(fn_pool)), replace=False)].sort_values("p", ascending=False)


def sev(v):
    if not isinstance(v, str):
        return "—"
    s = base_score(v)
    return f"{SEV[sev_rank(s)]} {s}"


def case(i, cve, r):
    desc = " ".join(str(r.description).split())
    nvd = r.nvd_vector if isinstance(r.nvd_vector, str) else None
    return "\n".join([
        f"### {i}. {cve}",
        "",
        f"- Published {r.published} · scorer `{r.cna}` ({r.score_source}) · CNA CWE {r.cna_cwe or '—'}",
        f"- Band **{r.band}** (stack p_bump {r.p:.3f}; likely ≥ {tau:.3f}, gate ≥ {gate_t:.3f})",
        "",
        "| | Vector | Severity |",
        "|---|---|---|",
        f"| CNA | `{r.cna_vector}` | {sev(r.cna_vector)} |",
        f"| NVD | `{nvd}` | {sev(nvd)} |" if nvd else
        "| NVD | — (kept the CNA vector; label = CNA) | — |",
        f"| Ours (served) | `{r.our_vector}` | {sev(r.our_vector)} |",
        f"| Fine-tuned LLM (raw) | `{r.llm_vector}` | {sev(r.llm_vector)} |",
        "",
        f"> {desc}",
        "",
        "Tag: ",
        "",
    ])


lines = [
    "# Error analysis sample (served combined model, 2026 evaluation rows)",
    "",
    f"Evaluation snapshot: NVD data as of {AS_OF}. Model: {serving['model']}, from `{a.preds}`. Rows: the "
    f"{len(d):,} 2026 test CVEs with a fine-tuned-LLM prediction (base rate {y.mean():.3f}). Generated by "
    "`scripts/10_error_analysis.py` (random sample, seed 0; within each section sorted by p_bump).",
    "",
    f"- **False positives:** band \"likely\" (p ≥ τ = {tau:.3f}) but NVD did not raise the band: "
    f"{len(fp_pool)} of {int((d.band == 'likely').sum())} \"likely\" rows; {len(fp)} sampled.",
    f"- **False negatives:** NVD raised the band but our band is not \"likely\": {len(fn_pool)} of {int(y.sum())} "
    f"raised rows ({int((fn_pool.band == 'possible').sum())} \"possible\", "
    f"{int((fn_pool.band == 'unlikely').sum())} \"unlikely\"); {len(fn)} sampled "
    f"({int((fn.band == 'possible').sum())} \"possible\", {int((fn.band == 'unlikely').sum())} \"unlikely\").",
    "- **Ours (served)** = the fine-tuned LLM vector if p ≥ the gate threshold, otherwise the CNA vector.",
    "",
    "**Tag each case [HUMAN]** with one of: `model wrong` / `NVD worst-casing` / `ambiguous description` / "
    "`label noise`.",
    "",
    "## False positives (flagged \"likely\", NVD did not raise)",
    "",
]
lines += [case(i, c, r) for i, (c, r) in enumerate(fp.iterrows(), 1)]
lines += ["## False negatives (NVD raised, not flagged \"likely\")", ""]
lines += [case(i, c, r) for i, (c, r) in enumerate(fn.iterrows(), len(fp) + 1)]
Path(a.out).write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
print(f"wrote {a.out}: {len(fp)} FP (pool {len(fp_pool)}), {len(fn)} FN (pool {len(fn_pool)})")

"""`patchsloth` CLI (SPEC §11.1)."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import typer

from . import config

app = typer.Typer(help="Patch Sloth: a second opinion on CNA-only CVSS scores for the CVEs in your lockfile.",
                  no_args_is_help=True)
feed_app = typer.Typer(help="Build the nightly second-opinion feed.", no_args_is_help=True)
app.add_typer(feed_app, name="feed")


@app.command()
def scan(path: Path = typer.Argument(..., exists=True, help="Lockfile or project directory"),
         format: str = typer.Option("md", "--format", "-f", help="md | json"),
         no_llm: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-llm", help="No LLM calls: NullBackend + template report"),
         no_report: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-report", help="Rows only, no report"),
         engine: str = typer.Option("auto", help="auto | osv | fallback"),
         fetch_missing: bool = typer.Option(False, help="Fetch CVEs missing from the feed from the NVD API")):
    """Scan a lockfile or a project directory."""
    from . import service
    from .feed import Feed
    from .llm.backends import get_backend

    files = [path] if path.is_file() else [p for n in ("package-lock.json", "requirements.txt")
                                           if (p := path / n).exists()]
    if not files:
        raise typer.BadParameter(f"no package-lock.json or requirements.txt in {path}")
    feed = Feed()
    if feed.df is None:
        typer.echo("warning: no feed found; run `patchsloth feed build` first", err=True)
    backend = get_backend("null" if no_llm else None)
    for f in files:
        res = service.run(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), f.name, feed, write=not no_report,
                          use_llm=False if no_llm else None, engine=engine, fetch_missing=fetch_missing,
                          backend=backend)
        if format == "json":
            typer.echo(json.dumps(res, indent=1, default=str))
        elif no_report:
            for r in res["rows"]:
                typer.echo(f"{r['bucket']}  {r['cve']:<18} {r['package']}@{r['version']}  {'; '.join(r['reason'])}")
        else:
            typer.echo(res["report_md"])
        typer.echo(f"[{f.name}: {res['n_deps']} deps, engine={res['engine']}, writer={res['costs']['writer']}, "
                   f"cost=${res['costs']['usd']:.4f}]", err=True)


@app.command()
def cve(cve_id: str = typer.Argument(..., help="e.g. CVE-2026-12345")):
    """Single-CVE second opinion."""
    from .service import cve_opinion
    res = cve_opinion(cve_id.upper())
    if res is None:
        typer.echo(f"{cve_id} not found in the feed or the NVD API", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(1)
    typer.echo(json.dumps(res, indent=1, default=str))


@feed_app.command("build")
def feed_build(since: str = typer.Option(None, help="Only CVEs published on/after YYYY-MM-DD in the CSV"),
               no_llm: bool = typer.Option(True, "--no-llm/--llm", help="HGB-only (CPU) or with the LLM backend"),
               model: str = typer.Option("hgb", help="Bump model saved by scripts/15 or 17 (hgb | tabpfn | stack)"),
               backend: str = typer.Option(None, help="LLM backend with --llm (e.g. precomputed)"),
               tabular_model: str = typer.Option("tabpfn", help="Scores rows without an LLM vector (stack only)")):
    """Score unanalysed CVEs and write feed/second_opinion.parquet + feed/latest.csv.
    Rebuild data/cves.parquet first with scripts/01_download.py and scripts/02_build_dataset.py."""
    from .feed import build
    typer.echo(json.dumps(build(since=since, model_name=model, no_llm=no_llm, backend_name=backend,
                                       tabular_model=tabular_model), indent=1, default=float))

    uvicorn.run("patchsloth.api:app", host=host, port=port)

def download_latest_release(repo: str = config.FEED_REPO, out_dir: Path = config.FEED,
                            models_dir: Path = config.MODELS, timeout: float = 60) -> str | None:
    """Fetch the newest GitHub release tagged feed-* into out_dir (the HGB fallback model goes to models_dir).
    Skips the download when out_dir already holds that tag. Returns the tag in use, or None on failure; the app
    then serves whatever local feed it has. Trust: bump_hgb.joblib is unpickled, so only point
    PATCHSLOTH_FEED_REPO at a repo you control."""
    out_dir, models_dir = Path(out_dir), Path(models_dir)
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(f"https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases?per_page=30",
                                     headers={"Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            rels = [r for r in json.load(resp) if r["tag_name"].startswith("feed-") and not r.get("draft")]
        if not rels:
            return None
        rel = max(rels, key=lambda r: (r["tag_name"], r["published_at"] or ""))
        tag_file = out_dir / "release_tag.txt"
        have = tag_file.read_text().strip() if tag_file.exists() else None
        if have == rel["tag_name"] and (out_dir / FEED_FILE.name).exists():
            return rel["tag_name"]
        assets = {x["name"]: x["browser_download_url"] for x in rel["assets"]}
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        models_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for name in config.FEED_ASSETS:
            if name not in assets:
                continue
            dest = (models_dir if name.endswith(".joblib") else out_dir) / name
            tmp = dest.with_suffix(dest.suffix + ".part")
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(assets[name], tmp)
            tmp.replace(dest)
        tag_file.write_text(rel["tag_name"] + "\n")
        return rel["tag_name"]
    except Exception as e:  # offline or rate-limited: keep serving the local feed
        print(f"feed download from {repo} failed: {e}")
        return None

"""Weight lifecycle utilities for Tinker training.
Provides functions for downloading, building, and publishing trained model
weights. Two build paths are available:
- :func:`build_hf_model` — merge LoRA adapter into a full HF model
- :func:`build_lora_adapter` — convert to PEFT format for serving with
  vLLM / SGLang (no merging, lightweight output)
Each function takes local paths as input/output, making them composable
and independently testable.
Example — merged model::
    from tinker_cookbook import weights
    adapter_dir = weights.download(
        tinker_path="tinker://run-id/sampler_weights/final",
        output_dir="./adapter",

    weights.build_hf_model(

        adapter_path=adapter_dir,
        output_path="./model",

    weights.build_lora_adapter(
        base_model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
        adapter_path=adapter_dir,
        output_path="./peft_adapter",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- osv-scanner
def osv_available() -> bool:
    return shutil.which("osv-scanner") is not None


def _osv_fixed(vuln: dict, ecosystem: str, name: str, version: str) -> str | None:
    for aff in vuln.get("affected", []):
        pkg = aff.get("package", {})
        if pkg.get("ecosystem") == ecosystem and pkg.get("name") == name:
            hit, fixed = _affected(ecosystem, version, aff)
            if hit and fixed:
                return fixed
    return None


def parse_osv_json(j: dict) -> list[Finding]:
    out = []
    for res in j.get("results") or []:
        for p in res.get("packages") or []:
            pkg = p["package"]
            eco, name, ver = pkg.get("ecosystem"), pkg.get("name"), pkg.get("version")
            for v in p.get("vulnerabilities") or []:
                ids = [v["id"], *v.get("aliases", [])]
                cves = sorted({x for x in ids if x.startswith("CVE-")})
                out.append(Finding(eco, name, ver, v["id"], cves, _osv_fixed(v, eco, name, ver),
                                   v.get("summary", ""), v.get("aliases", [])))
    return out


def run_osv(lockfile: Path, offline: bool = True) -> list[Finding]:
    """osv-scanner v2 on one lockfile. Exit code 1 means 'vulnerabilities found', not failure."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        out = Path(td) / "osv.json"
        cmd = ["osv-scanner", "scan", "source", "--format", "json", "--output-file", str(out), "-L", str(lockfile)]
        if offline:
            # --offline also stops transitive resolution via deps.dev (it sends the dependency list out)
            cmd[3:3] = ["--offline", "--offline-vulnerabilities"]
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode not in (0, 1) or not out.exists():
            raise RuntimeError(f"osv-scanner failed ({r.returncode}): {r.stderr[-500:]}")
        return parse_osv_json(json.loads(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- entry point
def scan_text(text: str, filename: str, engine: str = "auto", index: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Scan lockfile content. engine: auto | osv | fallback. Returns deps count, engine and findings."""
    deps = parse_lockfile(text, filename)
    used = engine
    findings: list[Finding] | None = None
    if engine in ("auto", "osv") and osv_available() and index is None:
        try:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
                p = Path(td) / Path(filename).name
                p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
                findings, used = run_osv(p), "osv-scanner"
        except Exception:
            if engine == "osv":
                raise
    if findings is None:
        findings, used = match_fallback(deps, index if index is not None else load_index()), "ghsa-fallback"
    return dict(n_deps=len(deps), engine=used, findings=[asdict(f) for f in findings])


def scan_path(path: Path, engine: str = "auto") -> dict:
    """A lockfile, or a directory containing package-lock.json / requirements.txt."""
    path = Path(path)
    files = [path] if path.is_file() else [p for n in ("package-lock.json", "requirements.txt")
                                           if (p := path / n).exists()]
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no package-lock.json or requirements.txt in {path}")
    res = [scan_text(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), f.name, engine) for f in files]
    return dict(n_deps=sum(r["n_deps"] for r in res), engine=",".join(sorted({r["engine"] for r in res})),
                findings=[x for r in res for x in r["findings"]])

class VLLMBackend:
    """OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions on the GPU Droplet (deploy/vllm-droplet.sh), model="patchsloth".
    Same prompt as training: Qwen3's chat template with enable_thinking=False renders the same tokens as Tinker's
    qwen3_disable_thinking renderer (checked on 200 test rows, DECISIONS.md). Greedy, max_tokens 48; parse failures
    fall back to the CNA vector, as in scripts/06. scripts/12_vllm_parity.py compares the outputs with Tinker's."""
    name = "vllm"

    def __init__(self, base_url: str = config.VLLM_BASE_URL, api_key: str = config.VLLM_API_KEY, client=None,
                 max_tokens: int = 48, concurrency: int = 8, timeout: float = 30):
        if not base_url and client is None:
            raise RuntimeError("VLLM_BASE_URL is not set")
        if client is None:
            from openai import OpenAI
            client = OpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key or "none", timeout=timeout, max_retries=1)
        self.client, self.max_tokens, self.concurrency = client, max_tokens, concurrency

    def complete(self, row) -> str:
        from .prompt import messages
        r = self.client.chat.completions.create(
            model=config.VLLM_MODEL, messages=messages(row), temperature=0, max_tokens=self.max_tokens,
            extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}})
        return r.choices[0].message.content or ""

    def predict_vectors(self, rows) -> list[str]:
        from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

        from .prompt import parse_output
        rows = list(rows)
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.concurrency) as ex:
            texts = list(ex.map(self.complete, rows))
        return [parse_output(t, r.cna_vector)[0] for t, r in zip(texts, rows)]

"""vLLM vs Tinker parity for the fine-tuned Qwen3-8B LoRA (SPEC §9.1 export, §12). Two steps:

  export   download the LoRA from Tinker and convert it to PEFT for vLLM (needs TINKER_API_KEY; downloads Qwen3-8B's
           config/weights from Hugging Face to map names). Run on the GPU Droplet, before deploy/vllm-droplet.sh serve.
             python scripts/12_vllm_parity.py export [--out peft_adapter]
  compare  send 300 random 2026 test CVEs (seed 0) to the vLLM server and compare with Tinker's outputs for the same
           CVEs (results/llm_preds_ft_test.jsonl, greedy, max_tokens 48). Writes results/vllm_parity.json.
             python scripts/12_vllm_parity.py compare --base_url http://<droplet>:8000/v1   (VLLM_API_KEY in env)

Two request modes are compared (each on the same 300 rows):
  tokens  /v1/completions with the exact prompt token IDs from Tinker's renderer (qwen3_disable_thinking) and
          <|im_end|> as the stop token: isolates the weights/kernels from prompt formatting.
  chat    /v1/chat/completions with chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=False: what VLLMBackend (the app) sends.
Greedy decoding on different kernels (Tinker vs vLLM, bf16) can still diverge, so the report gives exact-text match,
parsed-vector match, severity-band match and json_valid, not a pass/fail on exact text alone.
The vLLM parameter names (prompt as token IDs, stop_token_ids, chat_template_kwargs) are checked on 1 row first."""
import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from patchsloth.cvss import base_score, parse, severity  # noqa: E402
from patchsloth.llm.prompt import messages, parse_output  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("step", choices=["export", "compare"])
ap.add_argument("--model_path", default=None, help="tinker://... sampler weights (default: results/tinker_run.json)")
ap.add_argument("--out", default="peft_adapter")
ap.add_argument("--base_url", default=config.VLLM_BASE_URL)
ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=300)
ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=16)
ap.add_argument("--modes", default="tokens,chat")
a = ap.parse_args()
R = Path("results")

if a.step == "export":
    from dotenv import load_dotenv
    load_dotenv()
    from tinker_cookbook import weights
    path = a.model_path or json.loads((R / "tinker_run.json").read_text())["ft_path"]
    print("downloading", path)
    adapter = weights.download(tinker_path=path, output_dir="adapter_raw")
    weights.build_lora_adapter(base_model=config.BASE_MODEL, adapter_path=adapter, output_path=a.out)
    cfg = json.loads((Path(a.out) / "adapter_config.json").read_text())
    print(f"PEFT adapter in {a.out}: rank r={cfg.get('r')} (vllm serve needs --max-lora-rank >= r), "
          f"alpha={cfg.get('lora_alpha')}, targets={cfg.get('target_modules')}")
    sys.exit(0)

for line in open(R / "llm_preds_ft_test.jsonl", encoding="utf-8"):

df = pd.read_parquet(config.CVES_PARQUET).set_index("cve")
cves = sorted(c for c in tinker_text if c in df.index)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
sample = sorted(rng.choice(cves, size=min(a.n, len(cves)), replace=False))
rows = df.loc[sample].reset_index()
rows["description"] = rows.description.fillna("")


def call_tokens(r):
    ids = renderer.build_generation_prompt(messages(r)).to_ints()
    t0 = time.time()
    res = client.completions.create(model=config.VLLM_MODEL, prompt=ids, temperature=0, max_tokens=48,
                                    extra_body={"stop_token_ids": stop_ids, "skip_special_tokens": False})
    return res.choices[0].text, time.time() - t0


def call_chat(r):
    t0 = time.time()
    res = client.chat.completions.create(model=config.VLLM_MODEL, messages=messages(r), temperature=0, max_tokens=48,
                                         extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}})
    return res.choices[0].message.content or "", time.time() - t0


def clean(t):
    return t.replace("<|im_end|>", "").strip()


def band(v):
    return severity(base_score(parse(v))) if isinstance(v, str) else None


modes = {"tokens": call_tokens, "chat": call_chat}
first = next(rows.itertuples())
for m in a.modes.split(","):  # 1-row check of the request parameters before the batch
    print(m, "check:", repr(modes[m](first)[0][:120]))

out = {"base_url_host": a.base_url.split("//")[-1].split("/")[0].split(":")[0] and "redacted", "n": len(rows),
       "model": config.BASE_MODEL, "lora": "patchsloth", "data_as_of": (R / "data_as_of.txt").read_text().strip(),
       "tinker_source": "results/llm_preds_ft_test.jsonl (greedy, max_tokens 48)", "modes": {}}
for m in a.modes.split(","):
    t0 = time.time()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=a.concurrency) as ex:
        res = list(ex.map(modes[m], rows.itertuples()))
    wall = time.time() - t0
    exact = vec = sev = valid_v = valid_t = 0
    diffs = []
    for r, (text, _) in zip(rows.itertuples(), res):
        tt = tinker_text[r.cve]
        vv, ok_v = parse_output(text, r.cna_vector)
        vt, ok_t = parse_output(tt, r.cna_vector)
        exact += clean(text) == clean(tt)
        vec += vv == vt
        sev += band(vv) == band(vt)
        valid_v += ok_v
        valid_t += ok_t
        if vv != vt and len(diffs) < 10:
            diffs.append(dict(cve=r.cve, tinker=clean(tt), vllm=clean(text)))
    lat = np.array([s for _, s in res])
    n = len(rows)
    out["modes"][m] = dict(exact_text_match=exact / n, vector_match=vec / n, severity_match=sev / n,
                           json_valid_vllm=valid_v / n, json_valid_tinker=valid_t / n,
                           latency_s=dict(p50=float(np.percentile(lat, 50)), p95=float(np.percentile(lat, 95))),
                           wall_s=wall, concurrency=a.concurrency, rows_per_s=n / wall, first_diffs=diffs)
    print(m, json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out["modes"][m].items() if k != "first_diffs"}))
out.pop("base_url_host")
(R / "vllm_parity.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1))

<!--
Post skeleton (SPEC §17). Structure + facts only: every bullet is a number taken from a file in results/ (named in
brackets). Prose, hook, voice and personal parts are Ahmad's: [AHMAD: ...]. Image paths are relative to this file;
upload them to DEV before publishing. Evaluation snapshot: NVD data as of 2026-10-21T14:41Z unless a bullet says
otherwise; the live feed is release feed-2026-10-23 (data as of 2026-10-23).

# [AHMAD: title]

[AHMAD: cover image / tags: hf26challenge + partner tags]

## 1. Hook: NIST stopped checking

[AHMAD: hook, in your words. SPEC wording to riff on: "NIST stopped checking. Here's what that costs you."]

![Deferred CVEs per month](../results/charts/01_deferred_per_month.png)

- CVEs marked Deferred, by publication month: 1,465 in Mar 2026 → 5,768 in Sep 2026; 26,809 from Apr to 20 Oct 2026. [`results/charts/charts_data.json` → `deferred_per_month`]

## 2. The problem, with evidence

[AHMAD: framing paragraph]

![NVD own-score rate](../results/charts/02_nvd_own_score_rate.png)

- Of the CNA-scored CVEs NVD analysed, NVD wrote its own CVSS v3.1 vector for 94% (Jan 2024), 49% (Jan 2025), 38% (Jan 2026) and 12% (Sep 2026). [`charts_data.json` → `nvd_own_score_rate`]
- Where both NVD and the CNA scored (2025, n = 11,697), they disagreed on Confidentiality 49%, Integrity 43%, Availability 40% and Attack Vector 6% of the time. [`charts_data.json` → `field_disagreement`; chart `03_field_disagreement.png`]
- Across 122,459 labelled CVEs (2021–2026), NVD's label put 16.4% in a higher severity band than the scorer. [`charts_data.json` → `bump_rate_by_scorer`]
- Bump rate by scorer ranges from 77% (VulDB, n = 11,421) to 0.1% (Oracle, n = 4,711; Linux kernel, n = 3,810); CISA-ADP (Vulnrichment) 1.9% (n = 33,672). [same; chart `04_bump_rate_by_scorer.png`]

![Bump rate by scorer](../results/charts/04_bump_rate_by_scorer.png)

![Field disagreement](../results/charts/03_field_disagreement.png)

- Sources to cite for the policy change (SPEC §17; read before quoting): [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/?p=366659), [CSA research note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-nist-nvd-enrichment-overhaul-20260429-csa/), [VulnCheck on backlog exploitation](https://us-gov-east-1.vulncheck.com/blog/nvd-backlog-exploitation-lurking). [AHMAD: pick the facts you quote from these]
- Honesty framing (SPEC §2): NVD is not ground truth and tends to score the worst case ([Daniel Stenberg](https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2023/03/06/nvd-makes-up-vulnerability-severity-levels/)). The product says "an independent NVD-style reviewer would likely rate this higher", never "the vendor is wrong".

## 3. Who it's for

[AHMAD: personal: the lazy-but-responsible maintainer who ignores Dependabot because of alert fatigue]

## 4. Why it rewards laziness

[AHMAD: nobody re-scores 5,000 CVEs a month by hand, so the sloth does]

- The feed scores every unanalysed CVE nightly: 58,457 CVEs in release `feed-2026-10-23` (Deferred 49,272, Awaiting Analysis 6,604, Received 1,902, Undergoing Analysis 679). [`results/final_table.md` §6]

## 5. What I built

[AHMAD: architecture diagram, demo GIF, live URL]

## 6. How I know it works

### The headline

- When the served model said "likely under-rated", NIST had raised the band 75% of the time (281/376), vs a 9.5% base rate, on 8,000 2026 evaluation CVEs. The cut-off is label-free (top 10% of Deferred scores); it flags 4.7% of those rows. [`final_table.md` §7, `results/serving_stack.json`]

| Split | copy-CNA | base Qwen3-8B | fine-tuned Qwen3-8B |
|---|---|---|---|
| val (2025-H2) | 0.722 | 0.710 | **0.869** [0.861–0.876] |

- Gated override (use the LLM vector only when the stack is confident; threshold tuned on the last 3 months of val): test severity accuracy 0.899 vs copy-CNA 0.880, +2.0 points [1.5, 2.5] in all 3 seeds. [§4]

### Task B (rank CVEs NVD would raise; PR-AUC on 8,000 test rows, base rate 0.095) [`final_table.md` §2]

| Model (training rows) | PR-AUC (mean of 3 seeds) |
|---|---|
| copy-CNA | 0.095 |

"""Tabular features for the bump classifier, shared by training (scripts/07) and serving (feed, api).

Leakage rules (SPEC §8.4): every feature must be computable for a Deferred CVE on the day it was
published. FeatureBuilder only ever reads INPUT_COLUMNS; tests/test_features.py checks that none of
them is in FORBIDDEN. TF-IDF/SVD and the top-k category vocabularies are fitted on train only.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.decomposition import TruncatedSVD
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer

from .cvss import METRICS, VALUES, base_score, parse

# NVD-side or post-analysis information, plus the labels themselves
FORBIDDEN = {
    "status", "nvd_vector", "nvd_cwe", "nvd_ref_tags", "configurations", "has_cpe", "kev_date",
    "label_vector", "label_score", "label_sev", "bump_up", "vector_changed", "nvd_own", "split",
}
INPUT_COLUMNS = ["cna", "cna_vector", "cna_cwe", "score_source", "description", "n_refs",
                 "ref_github", "ref_exploitdb", "has_v40"]
LLM_INPUT = "llm_vector"  # optional, only with with_llm=True; must come from out-of-SFT predictions


def _first_cwe(s: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    return s.fillna("").astype(str).str.split(";").str[0]


class FeatureBuilder:
    """fit(train_df) then transform(any_df). transform is row-wise, so train/serve features match."""

    def __init__(self, top_k: int = 40, n_text: int = 32, with_llm: bool = False, min_df: int = 5):
        self.top_k, self.n_text, self.with_llm, self.min_df = top_k, n_text, with_llm, min_df

    def fit(self, train: pd.DataFrame) -> "FeatureBuilder":
        top_cna = list(train.cna.value_counts().index[:self.top_k])
        top_cwe = list(_first_cwe(train.cna_cwe).value_counts().index[:self.top_k])
        # sorted vocab with "other" reproduces the pd.Categorical codes the original 07 used
        self.cna_vocab = sorted(set(top_cna) | {"other"})
        self.cwe_vocab = sorted(set(top_cwe) | {"other"})
        self.tfidf = TfidfVectorizer(min_df=self.min_df, max_features=30000, sublinear_tf=True).fit(train.description)

def frame(split, seed):
    v = vecs("ft", split)
    rows = list(v)
    dd = df.loc[rows]
    return pd.DataFrame({"p": m4("tabpfn_llm_stack", seed).loc[rows].to_numpy(),

                         "lab_sev": dd.label_sev.to_numpy(), "y": dd.bump_up.astype(bool).to_numpy(),
                         "published": dd.published.to_numpy()}, index=rows)


def gate(f, t):
    over = f.p.to_numpy() >= t
    fsev = np.where(over, f.llm_sev, f.cna_sev)
    ok = fsev == f.lab_sev.to_numpy()
    yhat = fsev > f.cna_sev.to_numpy()
    y = f.y.to_numpy()
    tp = (yhat & y).sum()
    return dict(t=float(t), override_rate=float(over.mean()), severity_acc=float(ok.mean()),
                bump_precision=float(tp / max(yhat.sum(), 1)), bump_recall=float(tp / max(y.sum(), 1))), ok


def sweep(f):
    ts = np.unique(np.concatenate([[np.inf], np.quantile(f.p, np.linspace(0, 1, 201))]))
    return [gate(f, t)[0] for t in ts]


def paired_acc(ok_a, ok_b, seed=0):

"""Error analysis (SPEC §10): 20 false-positive "likely" flags and 20 false negatives on the 2026 evaluation test rows
(the 8,000 test CVEs with a fine-tuned-LLM prediction, frozen snapshot results/data_as_of.txt). Writes
results/error_sample.md for the human to tag [HUMAN].

Two sources (--model):
  hgb_llm_stack  (default, CPU) HistGBT + fine-tuned-LLM features trained on the 10k out-of-SFT stack_train rows,
                 seed 0: the M4 config `hgb_llm_stack` (scripts/12), refitted here from committed LLM predictions.
                 Bands and the gate are re-derived for THIS model with the served model's rules: likely >= q90 and
                 possible >= q75 of its p_bump over the Deferred CVEs with an LLM vector (label-free); gate t
                 maximises severity accuracy on the last 3 months of val (scripts/14's rule).
  served         the served stack (TabPFN-3.5 + LLM features, seed 0) from data/m4/tabpfn_llm_stack_s0.parquet
                 (scripts/12, GPU) with serving_stack.json's bands and gate; band counts are checked against it.

  false positive  band "likely" and NVD did NOT raise the band
  false negative  NVD raised the band, but the band is not "likely" (shown: "possible" or "unlikely")
"Ours" = what the product would serve: the LLM vector if p >= gate t, else the CNA vector. The raw LLM vector is
shown too. Usage: python scripts/10_error_analysis.py [--model hgb_llm_stack|served] [--n 20]"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth.cvss import base_score, parse, sev_rank, severity  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--model", choices=["hgb_llm_stack", "served"], default="hgb_llm_stack")
ap.add_argument("--preds", default="data/m4/tabpfn_llm_stack_s0.parquet", help="per-row predictions (--model served)")
ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=20)
ap.add_argument("--out", default="results/error_sample.md")
a = ap.parse_args()

R = Path("results")
AS_OF = (R / "data_as_of.txt").read_text().strip()
llm = {}
for s in ["stack_train", "val", "test", "unanalysed"]:
    llm.update(json.loads((R / f"llm_vectors_ft_{s}.json").read_text()))
df = pd.read_parquet("data/cves.parquet")


def vsev(v):
    return sev_rank(base_score(parse(v))) if isinstance(v, str) else np.nan


if a.model == "served":
    if not Path(a.preds).exists():
        sys.exit(f"{a.preds} not found: it is written by scripts/12_m4_experiments.py (config tabpfn_llm_stack, "
                 "seed 0) on a GPU. See deploy/RUNBOOK.md.")
    serving = json.loads((R / "serving_stack.json").read_text())
    tau, tau_possible, gate_t = serving["tau"], serving["tau_possible"], serving["gate_t"]
    pr = pd.read_parquet(a.preds)
    pr = pr[pr.split == "test"]
    p_test = pd.Series(pr.p.to_numpy(), index=pr.cve)
    model_desc = f"{serving['model']} (the served model), from `{a.preds}`"
    rules = "bands and gate from `results/serving_stack.json`"
    check_bands = {b: v["n"] for b, v in serving["test_eval_rows"]["bands"].items()}
    extra = {}
else:
    from patchsloth import tabular
    from patchsloth.features import LLM_INPUT, FeatureBuilder
    d0 = df[df.split.isin(["train", "val", "test", "deferred_unlabeled"])].copy()
    d0[LLM_INPUT] = d0.cve.map(llm)
    has = d0[LLM_INPUT].notna()
    train = d0.split == "train"
    # as scripts/12: vocabularies/TF-IDF fitted on all train rows, model on the train rows with an LLM vector
    fb = FeatureBuilder(with_llm=True).fit(d0[train])
    X, y = fb.transform(d0), d0.bump_up
    idx = d0[train & has].index
    clf = tabular.fit("hgb", X.loc[idx], y.loc[idx].astype(int), seed=0)

    def score(mask):
        m = mask.to_numpy()
        return pd.Series(tabular.predict_proba(clf, X[m]), index=d0.cve[m].to_numpy())

    p_test = score((d0.split == "test") & has)
    p_val = score((d0.split == "val") & has)
    p_def = score((d0.split == "deferred_unlabeled") & has)
    tau, tau_possible, tau_high = (float(np.quantile(p_def, q)) for q in (0.90, 0.75, 0.95))
    # gate: scripts/14's rule on the last 3 months of val (labels of val only)
    v = df.set_index("cve").loc[p_val.index]
    recent = v.published >= str((pd.Timestamp(v.published.max()) - pd.DateOffset(months=3)).date())
    fv = pd.DataFrame({"p": p_val, "llm_sev": [vsev(llm[c]) for c in p_val.index], "cna_sev": v.cna_sev,
                       "lab_sev": v.label_sev})[recent.to_numpy()]
    ts = np.unique(np.concatenate([[np.inf], np.quantile(fv.p, np.linspace(0, 1, 201))]))

    def acc(t):

bands = {b: dict(n=int((d.band == b).sum()), observed_bump_rate=float(y[d.band == b].mean())) for b in
         ["likely", "possible", "unlikely"]}

fp_pool = d[(d.band == "likely") & ~y]
fn_pool = d[y & (d.band != "likely")]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
fp = fp_pool.loc[rng.choice(fp_pool.index, size=min(a.n, len(fp_pool)), replace=False)].sort_values("p", ascending=False)

    s = base_score(parse(v))

def case(i, cve, r):

        f"- Band **{r.band}** (p_bump {r.p:.3f}; likely ≥ {tau:.3f}, gate ≥ {gate_t:.3f})",
        "",
        "| | Vector | Severity |",
        "|---|---|---|",
        f"| CNA | `{r.cna_vector}` | {sev(r.cna_vector)} |",
        f"| NVD | `{nvd}` | {sev(nvd)} |" if nvd else

        f"| Ours (served rule) | `{r.our_vector}` | {sev(r.our_vector)} |",
        f"| Fine-tuned LLM (raw) | `{r.llm_vector}` | {sev(r.llm_vector)} |",
        "",
        f"> {desc}",
        "",
        "Tag: ",
        "",
    ])

if a.model == "hgb_llm_stack":

"""Sanity check behind chart 04's VulDB bar (77% of VulDB-scored labelled CVEs put in a higher band by NVD):
5 random bumped examples (description, VulDB vector, NVD vector), the rate by year and split, and which CVSS fields
NVD changed on the bumped rows. Same rows and scorer rule as scripts/08 (score_source CNA, cna = cna@vuldb.com).
Writes results/vuldb_check.md. Usage: python scripts/18_vuldb_check.py"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth.cvss import METRICS, base_score, parse, severity  # noqa: E402

R = Path("results")
AS_OF = (R / "data_as_of.txt").read_text().strip()
df = pd.read_parquet("data/cves.parquet")
lab = df[df.split.isin(["train", "val", "test"])]
v = lab[(lab.cna == "cna@vuldb.com") & (lab.score_source != "CISA-ADP")].copy()
v["bump"] = v.bump_up.astype(bool)
v["year"] = v.published.str[:4]
bumped = v[v.bump]


def sev(x):
    s = base_score(parse(x))
    return f"{severity(s)} {s}"


changes = {f: float(np.mean([parse(c)[f] != parse(n)[f] for c, n in zip(bumped.cna_vector, bumped.label_vector)]))
           for f in METRICS}
pairs = pd.Series([f"{sev(c).split()[0]} → {sev(n).split()[0]}" for c, n in zip(bumped.cna_vector, bumped.label_vector)])
cia = pd.Series(["/".join(parse(c)[f] for f in "CIA") + " → " + "/".join(parse(n)[f] for f in "CIA")
                 for c, n in zip(bumped.cna_vector, bumped.label_vector)])
by_year = v.groupby("year").bump.agg(["size", "mean"])
by_split = v.groupby("split").bump.agg(["size", "mean"]).reindex(["train", "val", "test"])
ex = bumped.sample(5, random_state=0).sort_values("published")

L = ["# VulDB sanity check (chart 04: 77% bump rate)", "",
     f"Data as of {AS_OF}. Rows: labelled CVEs (train+val+test, SPEC §8.2 label rule) whose vector came from VulDB "
     f"(`cna@vuldb.com`, not CISA-ADP), as in `scripts/08_backlog_charts.py`. Generated by "
     "`scripts/18_vuldb_check.py`.", "",
     f"- VulDB-scored labelled CVEs: {len(v):,}; NVD put {len(bumped):,} ({v.bump.mean():.1%}) in a higher band.",
     f"- Every bumped row has an NVD-written vector: {int(bumped.nvd_vector.notna().sum()):,} of {len(bumped):,} "
     "(a bump needs NVD's own vector by the label rule).", "",
     "## Rate by year and split", "", "| | n | bump rate |", "|---|---|---|"]
L += [f"| {y} | {int(r['size']):,} | {r['mean']:.1%} |" for y, r in by_year.iterrows()]
L += [f"| split {s} | {int(r['size']):,} | {r['mean']:.1%} |" for s, r in by_split.iterrows()]
L += ["", "## What NVD changed on the bumped rows", "",
      "Share of bumped rows where NVD's value differs from VulDB's, per field:", "",
      "| " + " | ".join(METRICS) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(METRICS),
      "| " + " | ".join(f"{changes[f]:.0%}" for f in METRICS) + " |", "",
      "Most common severity changes: " + "; ".join(f"{k} {n:,}" for k, n in pairs.value_counts().head(4).items()) + ".",
      "", "Most common C/I/A changes (VulDB → NVD): " +
      "; ".join(f"`{k}` {n:,}" for k, n in cia.value_counts().head(5).items()) + ".", "",
      "## 5 random bumped examples (seed 0)", ""]
for i, (_, r) in enumerate(ex.iterrows(), 1):
    L += [f"### {i}. {r.cve} (published {r.published}, CWE {r.cna_cwe or '—'})", "",
          "| | Vector | Severity |", "|---|---|---|",
          f"| VulDB | `{r.cna_vector}` | {sev(r.cna_vector)} |",
          f"| NVD | `{r.nvd_vector}` | {sev(r.nvd_vector)} |", "",
          "> " + " ".join(str(r.description).split()), ""]
(R / "vuldb_check.md").write_text("\n".join(L), encoding="utf-8")
print("\n".join(L[:30]))

    && ls -la /out && rm -rf /tmp/adb

input.content:
# App Platform deploy (Option B): morning steps

Goal: the API and web page live on DigitalOcean App Platform, with no GPU. One service, `apps-s-1vcpu-2gb`
($25/month, billed per second). Spec: `deploy/do-app.yaml`. Image: `deploy/Dockerfile`.

What the image contains, so start-up never depends on the GitHub API:
- the feed release `feed-2026-10-23` (parquet, CSV, meta, HGB fallback model);
- the GHSA advisory index, built during the image build from the latest GitHub Advisory DB;
- osv-scanner 2.7.0 and its npm/PyPI offline DB.

The deployed app scans with the in-process GHSA index (`PATCHSLOTH_SCAN_ENGINE=fallback`). Measured on the laptop,
an offline osv-scanner run takes 26–39 s and ~0.6 GB per lockfile, because it reloads its database on every call.
The fallback matcher agreed with osv-scanner on both fixture lockfiles (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-21).

The DigitalOcean console labels below are written from the docs and may differ slightly on screen. The field
values are exact.

## 0. Before you start (laptop, 1 min)

```bash
cd ~/Downloads/TECH_PROJECTS/hacktoberFestweek3/patch-sloth
git pull && git log -1 --oneline     # the commit that added deploy/DEPLOY_STEPS.md, or newer
date -u +%FT%TZ                      # note this: app creation time, for the cost table
```

## 1. Create the app (console, ~5 min)

1. Go to <https://cloud.digitalocean.com>, click **Create** (top right), then **App Platform**.
2. Source: choose **GitHub**. If asked, click **Authorize / Install** the DigitalOcean GitHub app. Choose
   **Only select repositories** → `MAUK9086/patch-sloth` → **Install**.
3. Repository `MAUK9086/patch-sloth`, branch `master`, **Source directory** `patch-sloth`, **Autodeploy** on.
   Click **Next**.
4. DigitalOcean looks for a Dockerfile in the source directory, but ours is in `deploy/`. Pick one of these:
   - On the resources screen, edit the component: set **Build strategy / Resource type** to **Dockerfile**, and
     **Dockerfile path** to `patch-sloth/deploy/Dockerfile`. Set **HTTP port** to `8080`.
   - Or, simplest: continue with whatever it detects. After step 9, open **Settings → App Spec → Edit**, paste
     the whole of `deploy/do-app.yaml`, click **Save**, and it redeploys with the right settings.
5. **Size:** Basic / shared CPU, **1 vCPU, 2 GB** (`apps-s-1vcpu-2gb`, $25/mo), 1 container.
   Do not pick 1 GB: the app uses ~0.6 GB with the feed loaded.
6. **Environment variables** (component level). Add the plain ones exactly as in `deploy/do-app.yaml`:
   | Key | Value |
   |---|---|
   | `PATCHSLOTH_FEED_REPO` | `MAUK9086/patch-sloth` |
   | `PATCHSLOTH_FEED_DOWNLOAD` | `1` |
   | `PATCHSLOTH_SCAN_ENGINE` | `fallback` |
   | `PATCHSLOTH_LLM_BACKEND` | `null` |

   Then add `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY` = your key, with the **Encrypt** box ticked. Without it, reports use the
   template writer, which is fine but has no Ultramarine.
7. **Health check:** HTTP, path `/health`, initial delay 30 s, period 10 s, timeout 10 s, failure threshold 12.
   This is already in the spec if you used the paste route.
8. **Region:** New York (`nyc`). **App name:** `patch-sloth`.
9. Click **Create Resources** / **Create App**.

## 2. Watch the build (~10–15 min)

Open the app → **Activity** → the running deployment → **Build logs**. Expected milestones, in order:
- `git clone ... advisory-database` and then `ls -la /out` showing `advisory_index.json.gz` (a few MB);
- `pip install` of `requirements-app.txt`;
- `osv-scanner ... --download-offline-databases`, then `du -sh /opt/osv-db` printing about 245M;
- 4 `curl` downloads of the feed into `/app/feed` and `/app/data/models`;
- `Successfully built`, then the deploy phase, with health checks on `/health`.

## 3. Check it works (laptop, 2 min)

```bash
APP=https://patch-sloth-xxxxx.ondigitalocean.app     # <- paste the app URL from the console
curl -s "$APP/health"; echo
# expected: "status":"ok", "model":"stack", "feed_rows":240071, "scan_engine":"fallback",
#           "feed_release":"feed-2026-10-23" (or "feed-2026-10-23 (local copy)" if GitHub was unreachable)
curl -s -F "file=@patch-sloth/tests/fixtures/package-lock.json" -F "no_llm=true" "$APP/scan" | head -c 600; echo
curl -s -F "file=@patch-sloth/tests/fixtures/requirements.txt" "$APP/scan" | python -c "import json,sys; j=json.load(sys.stdin); print(j['engine'], len(j['rows']), j['costs'])"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" "$APP/feed/latest.csv"
```
Then open `$APP` in a browser, paste a lockfile, and take the screenshot for the post.

## 4. If something fails

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Build log: "Dockerfile not found" or a buildpack build | Dockerfile path not set | Step 1.4: Settings → App Spec → paste `deploy/do-app.yaml` |
| Build fails at `osv-scanner ... warm-up failed` | network hiccup while downloading the OSV DB | **Actions → Force rebuild and deploy** |
| Build fails at `git clone advisory-database` | GitHub hiccup | Force rebuild |
| Deploy: health check failed, runtime log shows `Killed` / OOM | memory | Settings → component → size **2 vCPU / 4 GB** (`apps-s-2vcpu-4gb`, $50/mo) |
| Health check failed, no OOM | slow cold start | raise `initial_delay_seconds` to 90 in the spec |
| `/health` shows `"feed_release": "... (local copy)"` | GitHub API rate limit at boot | harmless: the baked feed is served |
| `/scan` returns 503 "scanner unavailable" | the advisory index is missing from the image | check the build log for the `/out` listing; force rebuild |

## 5. Costs to record (for the post's cost table)

- App creation time (step 0) and, if you delete it later, the deletion time.
- The plan: `apps-s-1vcpu-2gb`, $25/month ≈ $0.034/hour, billed per second, 1-minute minimum
  (docs.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform/details/pricing, checked 2026-10-24).

# GPU window (Option A): one Droplet session, at most 2.5 hours

One NVIDIA **L40S** GPU Droplet (48 GB; $1.57/hour on demand, billed per second, **still billed when powered off**
until destroyed; DigitalOcean pricing page, checked 2026-10-24). Worst case 2.5 h ≈ $3.93.

Order: start-time log → firewall → vLLM with the LoRA → parity → rebuild the M4 stack predictions (TabPFN) →
error analysis on the served model → latency → copy results to the laptop, commit, push → destroy → stop-time log.

vLLM is capped at half the GPU (`GPU_MEM_UTIL=0.5`, ~24 GB), so TabPFN can run in the same session without stopping
it. Everything runs **on the Droplet against localhost**. Port 8000 is open only to your laptop's IP, never to the
internet.

Conventions:
- **[laptop]** blocks run in Git Bash in `~/Downloads/TECH_PROJECTS/hacktoberFestweek3/patch-sloth`.
- **[droplet]** blocks run in the SSH session.
- Secrets are typed at hidden `read -s` prompts, so they never land in shell history or files.

**Hard stop.** At **T+2:15**, skip whatever is left and go straight to steps 9–10. The budget column is a guide.

| Step | What | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Create the Droplet, log the start time | 0:00–0:10 |
| 1 | Firewall, clone, frozen data, secrets | 0:10–0:20 |
| 2 | vLLM + LoRA export (`deploy/vllm-droplet.sh`) | 0:20–0:45 |
| 3 | Parity, 300 CVEs (`12_vllm_parity.py compare`) | 0:45–0:55 |
| 4 | Rebuild the M4 stack predictions (TabPFN, seed 0) | 0:55–1:35 |
| 5 | Error analysis on the served model | 1:35–1:40 |
| 6 | Latency, 100 single-CVE requests | 1:40–1:50 |
| 7 | Copy results to the laptop | 1:50–2:00 |
| 8 | Commit and push (laptop) | 2:00–2:05 |
| 9 | Destroy the Droplet, log the stop time | 2:05–2:15 |

## Before the window (laptop)

- Have ready: `TINKER_API_KEY`, `TABPFN_TOKEN` (Prior Labs), and an SSH key added in DigitalOcean (**Settings →
  Security → SSH keys**). If TabPFN asks for Hugging Face access to the gated `Prior-Labs/tabpfn_3_5` weights, you
  will also need `HF_TOKEN` from the account that accepted those terms.
- The frozen evaluation data must be on the laptop: `patch-sloth/data/cves.parquet` (45 MB, data as of
  2026-10-21T14:41Z).

## 0. Create the Droplet and log the start (console + laptop)

Console: **Create → Droplets**. Choose **GPU Droplets**, a region with L40S capacity, then **NVIDIA L40S** (1 GPU).
For the image, pick the **AI/ML Ready** Ubuntu image (NVIDIA drivers preinstalled). Select your SSH key, name it
`patchsloth-gpu`, and click **Create GPU Droplet**. Copy its public IPv4.

```bash
# [laptop]
IP=203.0.113.10          # <- paste the Droplet's IPv4
mkdir -p patch-sloth/results
echo "{\"event\": \"droplet_created\", \"utc\": \"$(date -u +%FT%TZ)\", \"plan\": \"gpu-l40s-1x\", \"usd_per_hour\": 1.57}" >> patch-sloth/results/do_gpu_session.jsonl
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new root@$IP 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv'
```

## 1. Firewall, code, frozen data, secrets

```bash
# [droplet]  ssh root@<IP>
MY_IP=${SSH_CLIENT%% *}; echo "your laptop IP: $MY_IP"
ufw allow OpenSSH
```

the app sends). Each mode reports exact-text, vector and severity match, plus json_valid.

## 4. Rebuild the M4 per-row stack predictions (TabPFN-3.5 + LLM features, seed 0) (~30–40 min)

This uses a separate venv, so TabPFN's torch never touches vLLM's.

def get_model_state_keys(model_dir: Path) -> set[str]:
    """Get all weight key names from safetensors files without loading tensor data.

    Uses ``safetensors.safe_open`` to read headers only, which is fast and
    uses negligible memory regardless of model size.

    Args:
        model_dir: Directory containing ``.safetensors`` files.

    Returns:
        Set of all tensor key names across all shard files.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If no ``.safetensors`` files are found.
    """
    return set(get_model_state_shapes(model_dir).keys())


def get_model_state_shapes(model_dir: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Get shape for each weight key from safetensors headers without loading tensor data.

    Uses ``safetensors.safe_open`` to read headers only. This is fast and uses
    negligible memory regardless of model size. Useful for upfront shape
    validation before loading any weight shards.

    Args:
        model_dir: Directory containing ``.safetensors`` files.

    Returns:
        Dict mapping tensor key names to their shapes.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If no ``.safetensors`` files are found.
    """
    shard_files = sorted(model_dir.glob("*.safetensors"))
    if not shard_files:
        _raise_no_safetensors(model_dir)

    shapes: dict[str, tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    for sf_path in shard_files:
        with safe_open(str(sf_path), framework="pt") as f:
            for key in f.keys():  # noqa: SIM118 — safe_open doesn't support `in`
                shapes[key] = tuple(f.get_slice(key).get_shape())
    return shapes


def get_shard_files(model_dir: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Get sorted list of safetensors shard filenames in a model directory.

    Prefers reading ``model.safetensors.index.json`` for the canonical shard
    list. Falls back to globbing for ``.safetensors`` files.

    Args:
        model_dir: Directory containing the model shards.

    Returns:
        Sorted list of shard filenames (not full paths).

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If no ``.safetensors`` files are found.
    """
    index_path = model_dir / "model.safetensors.index.json"
    if index_path.exists():
        with open(index_path) as f:
            weight_map = json.load(f)["weight_map"]
        return sorted(set(weight_map.values()))

    shard_files = sorted(model_dir.glob("*.safetensors"))
    if not shard_files:
        _raise_no_safetensors(model_dir)
    return [f.name for f in shard_files]

def resolve_model_dir(base_model: str) -> Path:
    """Resolve a HuggingFace model name or local path to a local directory.

    If ``base_model`` is already a local directory, returns it directly.
    Otherwise downloads from HuggingFace Hub via ``snapshot_download``.

    Args:
        base_model: HuggingFace model name (e.g. ``"Qwen/Qwen3-8B"``) or
            local path to a model directory.

    Returns:
        Path to local directory containing model files.
    """
    if os.path.isdir(base_model):
        logger.info("Using local model directory: %s", base_model)
        return Path(base_model)

    from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

    logger.info("Downloading model files for %s", base_model)
    local_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id=base_model)
    return Path(local_dir)

# [AHMAD: title]

[AHMAD: cover image; tags: hf26challenge + partner tags]

## 1. Hook

[AHMAD: hook, in your words. SPEC line to riff on: "NIST stopped checking. Here's what that costs you."]

![Deferred CVEs per month](../results/charts/01_deferred_per_month.png)

In March 2026, 1,465 newly published CVEs were marked Deferred. In September it was 5,768. From April to 20
October 2026, the total was 26,809. [`results/charts/charts_data.json` → `deferred_per_month`]

## 2. The problem, with evidence

A Deferred CVE is one NIST's National Vulnerability Database (NVD) will not analyse. Its only severity score is the
one from the CNA, the organisation that reported it (often the vendor itself). [SPEC §1]

NVD's own review is also shrinking for the CVEs it does analyse. In January 2024, NVD wrote its own CVSS v3.1
vector for 94% of the analysed CVEs that had a CNA score. By January 2025 it was 49%, by January 2026 38%, and in
September 2026 12%. [`charts_data.json` → `nvd_own_score_rate`]

![NVD own-score rate](../results/charts/02_nvd_own_score_rate.png)

When both scored, they often disagreed. Among 2025 CVEs where NVD and the CNA both wrote a vector (11,697 CVEs),
they disagreed on Confidentiality 49% of the time, Integrity 43% and Availability 40%. Attack Vector, by contrast,
differed only 6% of the time. [`charts_data.json` → `field_disagreement`]

![Field disagreement](../results/charts/03_field_disagreement.png)

Across all 122,459 labelled CVEs from 2021 to 2026, NVD's label put 16.4% in a higher severity band than the scorer
had. The rate depends heavily on who scored the CVE. [`charts_data.json` → `bump_rate_by_scorer`]

![Bump rate by scorer](../results/charts/04_bump_rate_by_scorer.png)

- VulDB: 77% of 11,421 CVEs raised. Most of these are one pattern: VulDB scores C/I/A as Low/Low/Low and NVD as

NVD is not ground truth either. It tends to score the worst case, and Daniel Stenberg of curl has argued that it

CVE higher. Every output is an estimate for triage, not an official score.

## 3. Who it's for

[AHMAD: personal: the lazy-but-responsible maintainer who ignores Dependabot because of alert fatigue]

## 4. Why it rewards laziness

[AHMAD: nobody re-scores 5,000 CVEs a month by hand, so the sloth does]

The feed re-scores every unanalysed CVE in one batch. Release `feed-2026-10-23` covers 58,457 CVEs: 49,272
Deferred, 6,604 Awaiting Analysis, 1,902 Received and 679 Undergoing Analysis. [`results/final_table.md` §6]

## 5. What I built

[AHMAD: architecture diagram, demo GIF, live URL]

You give Patch Sloth a `package-lock.json` or a `requirements.txt`, and it works in four steps:
1. It finds the vulnerable packages and their CVE IDs.
2. It looks each CVE up in the precomputed feed.
3. It sorts the CVEs into P0 "patch now", P1 "this month" and P2 "ignore for now", using fixed rules: CISA KEV,
   EPSS ≥ 0.10, and the predicted severity when the model is confident.
4. Ultramarine 1 Flash writes a short report. A guardrail checks that every CVE ID and number in the report appears
   in the input; if not, the report is retried once and then replaced by a template. [SPEC §11]

There is a CLI, a web page and an API. For CVEs that NIST has already reviewed, the report shows the CNA and NVD
severities side by side and makes no prediction. [DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-23]

I scanned the current lockfiles of three popular npm projects without opening any issues. Their lockfiles include
dev, test and example dependencies, so a finding does not mean the published package is affected.
[`results/demo/README.md`]

| Project | Dependencies | CVEs | Deferred CVEs | Report cost | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| markedjs/marked | 625 | 14 | 8 | $0.0012 | pass |
| mochajs/mocha | 715 | 36 | 11 | $0.0024 | pass |
| socketio/socket.io | 1,212 | 112 | 22 | $0.0077 | pass |

[AHMAD: screenshot of a report on the web page]

## 6. Data and methods

**Data.** The dataset covers 239,058 non-rejected CVEs from 2021 to 2026, taken from NVD's JSON feeds (fkie-cad
mirror). It is split by publication date, never randomly. Train is before July 2025 (80,098 CVEs), validation is
2025-H2 (11,655) and test is 2026 (30,706). The 48,979 Deferred CVEs with a CNA score are the population the
product scores. [`results/dataset_summary.txt`]

**Label.** For a CVE that NVD analysed and the CNA scored, the label is NVD's vector if NVD wrote one. Otherwise
the label is the CNA's vector, because NVD reviewed it and kept it. A "bump" means the label's severity band is
higher than the CNA's. The bump rate is 18.2% in train, 22.7% in validation and 9.3% in test.
[SPEC §8.2, `results/dataset_summary.txt`]

**No leakage.** The features use only what is known about a Deferred CVE on the day it is published: the CNA's
vector, CWE and identity, the description, references and a CVSS v4 flag. NVD status, NVD's vector and CWE, CPE
configurations and KEV dates are never features. Text features are fitted on train only. [SPEC §8.4,
`tests/test_features.py`]

**Task A, predict NVD's vector.** Qwen3-8B, fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 32, learning rate 2e-4, batch 64, one
epoch) on 30,000 training CVEs on Tinker, with thinking turned off. The model sees the CNA, its CWE, its vector
and the description, and answers with eight CVSS fields as JSON. Training took 469 steps, and the logged loss fell
from 2.97 at step 10 to 0.97 at the last step. [`results/tinker_run.json`, `results/tinker_train_log.jsonl`]

**Task B, rank CVEs NVD would raise.** These models are binary classifiers for "NVD raised the band", scored by
PR-AUC on the same 8,000 2026 test CVEs:
- TabPFN-3.5, HistGBT and logistic regression on tabular features;
- a stacked model: TabPFN with the fine-tuned LLM's predictions as extra features, trained on 10,000 training CVEs
  that were held out from fine-tuning.

"Better" means the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of the difference excludes zero in each of 3 seeds.
[`results/final_table.md` §2]

**What users see.** Users get a band, not a probability. The cut-offs are quantiles of the model's own scores over
the Deferred CVEs, so no labels are used to choose them: "likely" is the top 10%, "possible" the next 15%.
[`results/serving_stack.json`]

## 7. Results

### Headline

When the served model said "likely under-rated", NIST had raised the band 75% of the time (281 of 376 CVEs). The
base rate on the same 8,000 2026 test CVEs is 9.5%. The "possible" band was confirmed 29% of the time and
"unlikely" 3.8%. [`results/serving_stack.json`, `final_table.md` §7]

### Predicting NVD's vector

Severity accuracy is the share of CVEs where the predicted vector falls in the same severity band as NVD's label.
[`final_table.md` §1]

| Split | Copy the CNA | Base Qwen3-8B | Fine-tuned Qwen3-8B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation (2025-H2) | 0.722 | 0.710 | **0.869** [0.861–0.876] |
| Test (2026) | **0.880** | 0.865 | 0.859 [0.851–0.866] |

On 2025-H2 the fine-tuned model beats copying the CNA clearly (McNemar p = 2e-143). On 2026 it does not: copying
the CNA is better (p = 2e-6), because in 2026 NVD changes far fewer CNA vectors.

The fine-tuned model is much better than the base model at spotting raises: bump F1 0.830 vs 0.033 on validation,
and 0.559 vs 0.108 on test. It produced valid JSON for 100% of CVEs. [`final_table.md` §1]

The fine-tune helps most on the fields CNAs and NVD dispute. On validation, accuracy on Confidentiality went from
0.749 (base) to 0.933, Integrity from 0.788 to 0.934 and Availability from 0.804 to 0.936.
[`results/llm_val.json`]

**Use the LLM only when the stack is confident.** The served vector is the LLM's when the stacked model's
probability is at least t, and the CNA's otherwise. With t tuned on the last three months of validation, this
changes 6% of 2026 CVEs. Severity accuracy is then 0.899, against 0.880 for copying the CNA: +2.0 points
[1.5, 2.5], in all 3 seeds. [`final_table.md` §4]

![Gated override](../results/gated_override.png)

### Ranking CVEs NVD would raise

PR-AUC on the 8,000 2026 test CVEs (base rate 0.095; mean of 3 seeds). [`final_table.md` §2]

| Model (training CVEs) | PR-AUC |
|---|---|
| Copy the CNA (never flags) | 0.095 |
| Fine-tuned Qwen3-8B alone | 0.404 |
| TF-IDF + logistic regression (all train) | 0.426 |
| TabPFN-3.5 + LLM features (10k) | 0.621 |
| HistGBT (all 80,098) | 0.627 |
| TabPFN-3.5 (50k) | 0.631 |

- TabPFN-3.5 on 50k CVEs and HistGBT on all 80k are not significantly different.
- The stacked model is far better at ranking than the LLM alone (+0.22).
- Adding the LLM's features helps HistGBT significantly (+0.035), but not TabPFN.

### TabPFN is about sample efficiency

![Learning curve](../results/learning_curve.png)

At 5,000 and 10,000 training CVEs, TabPFN beats HistGBT trained on the same CVEs by 0.05 to 0.08 PR-AUC, in every
seed. TabPFN on 5,000 CVEs reaches 0.602, against 0.627 for HistGBT on all 80,098. That is 96% of the way with
1/16 of the labels and no tuning, though the gap is still significant in 2 of 3 seeds. From 30,000 CVEs up, the
two are level. [`final_table.md` §8]

### The 2026 drift

![2026 drift](../results/charts/05_drift_2026.png)

NVD raised 18% of training-period CVEs, 23% in 2025-H2 and 9% in 2026. [`charts_data.json` →
`bump_rate_by_split`]

That shift breaks thresholds tuned on the past. One HistGBT model (all training CVEs) was given two thresholds:
- tuned on the last three months of validation to reach 50% precision: 28% precision on 2026, flagging 30% of
  CVEs;
- the label-free cut-off (top 10% of Deferred scores): 74% precision on 2026, flagging 4.4% of CVEs.

[`charts_data.json` → `tau_drift_hgb_all_train`]

The gate shows the same pattern. Tuned on all of 2025-H2 validation, it is 2.1 points worse than copying the CNA on
2026; tuned on the last three months, it is 2.0 points better. [`final_table.md` §4]

### Frontier zero-shot comparison

The same 1,000 test CVEs, scored by every model. [`final_table.md` §3, `results/frontier_1k.json`]

| Model | Severity accuracy | Cost per 1,000 CVEs |
|---|---|---|
| Copy the CNA | 0.874 | $0 |
| Base Qwen3-8B | 0.865 | $0.063 |
| Fine-tuned Qwen3-8B | 0.861 | $0.045 (+ $3.37 one-off training) |
| Ultramarine 1 Flash, zero-shot | 0.795 | $0.092 |

Zero-shot Ultramarine changes CNA vectors too often: it is significantly worse than copying the CNA (McNemar
p = 7e-11). On these 1,000 rows, the fine-tuned model and copy-the-CNA are not significantly different (p = 0.32).

## 9. What went wrong

**The baseline that was smaller than its name.** For three milestones, the "HistGBT, all training data" baseline
was actually trained on 10,000 rows: a command-line default meant for TabPFN applied to every model. Retrained on
all 80,098 rows, HistGBT scores 0.627, which removed most of TabPFN's accuracy lead. That is why the TabPFN result
is about sample efficiency, not accuracy. It was caught by an "anomaly" in which HistGBT on 30k rows beat HistGBT
on "all" rows. [`final_table.md` §9]

**The NaN label bug.** The label rule was first written as `nvd_vector or cna_vector`. In pandas a missing string
is NaN, and NaN counts as true. So every CVE that NVD had accepted unchanged lost its label, and the labelled set
held only CVEs NVD had rescored. The fix uses explicit string checks and added 7,367 labels (115,092 → 122,459).
A regression test covers None, NaN and `pd.NA`. [`final_table.md` §9, `tests/test_label_rule.py`]

**A test that only failed on Linux.** The advisory scanner read files in filesystem order, which is alphabetical
on Windows and hash order on Linux, so a test picked a different "fixed" version on each. The index is now built
from a sorted list. [`final_table.md` §9]

**An unfair comparison, fixed.** Ultramarine was first scored on 1,000 CVEs and compared with Qwen on 8,000. Every
model is now scored on the same 1,000. [`final_table.md` §3]

**Thresholds that don't survive 2026.** See the drift section. This turned from a bug into a finding.

[AHMAD: anything personal about these]

## 10. Limitations

- Every score is an estimate for triage, not an official CVSS score.
- The label is NVD's decision, and NVD tends to score the worst case.
- In 2026 NVD writes its own vector for far fewer CVEs (12% in September). Some "kept the CNA's score" labels may
  reflect less review rather than agreement.
- On 2026 CVEs, the fine-tuned model alone is less accurate than copying the CNA (0.859 vs 0.880). Only the gated
  version beats it.
- CVSS v3.1 only. npm and PyPI only. No affected-product (CPE) lists. EPSS is an input, and the product does not
  predict exploitation.
- The headline numbers use 8,000 of the 30,706 test CVEs: those with a fine-tuned prediction.
  [`final_table.md` intro]

**1. Error analysis.** `results/error_sample.md` has 20 false positives and 20 false negatives, each with an empty `Tag:` line for you.
- The cases come from the HGB + LLM-features stack, refitted on CPU from the committed LLM predictions. It scores 0.613 here vs 0.609 in M4, because 243 eval rows have slightly different CNA-side inputs between the two data snapshots.
- I changed one word in your note: no paired test was ever run between this stack and the served one, so instead of "tied" the file says their 95% CIs overlap (0.609 [0.573–0.643] vs 0.621 [0.584–0.655]). The rest of your wording is there, and it's logged in DECISIONS.md.

**2. VulDB check** (`results/vuldb_check.md`). The 77% is mostly one convention gap. In 5,850 of the 8,747 raised VulDB CVEs, VulDB scored C/I/A as Low/Low/Low and NVD as High/High/High; two thirds of those are SQL injection (CWE-89). VulDB's rate drops to 57.9% in 2026. The file has 5 random examples with their VulDB and NVD vectors.

**3. Deploy readiness.** The main problem was osv-scanner. I timed the offline mode here: each lockfile scan took 26–39 s and peaked at about 0.6 GB, because it reloads its database every time. Two of those at once would likely crash a 2 GB instance. Fixes:
- The image now builds the GitHub advisory index during the Docker build, and the app uses that by default (`PATCHSLOTH_SCAN_ENGINE=fallback`). osv-scanner stays in the image as an opt-in, limited to one scan at a time.
- The image includes the `feed-2026-10-23` release, so a GitHub rate limit at startup can't leave the app with no data.
- The app loads the feed before taking traffic instead of on the first health check, and the health check now allows about 2.5 minutes.
- A missing scanner database now gives a 503 instead of a crash.
- Secrets are out of `do-app.yaml`; you add them in the console as encrypted.

The Docker image is still untested: Docker isn't running here. `deploy/DEPLOY_STEPS.md` has the console clicks, the build-log lines to expect, curl checks, and a fix table for likely failures. The console labels are from DigitalOcean's docs and may differ slightly on screen.

**4. GPU runbook** (`deploy/RUNBOOK.md`). It covers the steps in your order, with a time budget per step and a hard stop at 2:15.
- Port 8000 is opened only to your laptop's IP.
- Keys are typed at hidden prompts, so they stay out of shell history.
- Start and stop times go to `results/do_gpu_session.jsonl`.
- Results are copied back with `scp` and committed from the laptop, so no GitHub credentials go on the Droplet.
- vLLM is capped at half the GPU so TabPFN can run alongside it.
- I added a latency mode to the parity script: 100 single-CVE requests, p50/p95.

TabPFN will need your `TABPFN_TOKEN`, and possibly an `HF_TOKEN` if the weights are gated.

**5. Parity fallback.** Your sentence says "weights exported in PEFT format", but that export had never actually been run, so I started it here (not a paid call). The draft marks that line `[PENDING]` until it finishes. Tinker's download call printed a deprecation warning; if Tinker rejects it, the sentence needs rewording and the runbook's export step needs a different download method.

**6. Post.** `post/draft.md` now has short factual paragraphs for the technical sections, each citing its source file. Your parts are still `[AHMAD: ...]`. The open TODOs are error-analysis tag counts, per-CNA model results (never computed), the DigitalOcean URL and costs, and vLLM parity.

When the export finishes, I'll write `results/peft_export.json`, clear the `[PENDING]` mark (or reword it if Tinker rejects the download), and push.
